title: A2 Writing Quiz 4 — Travel, Seasons & Staying Active

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Have you finished packing your bag yet?
Have you finish packing your bag yet?
Did you finished packing your bag yet?
Have you finished packing your bag already?
questions.explanation: 'Yet' is used in present perfect questions and negatives: 'Have you finished... yet?'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We have travelled to Gabala in 2022.
We travelled to Gabala in 2022.
We have travel to Gabala in 2022.
We are travelling to Gabala in 2022.
questions.explanation: A finished past year ('in 2022') needs past simple, not present perfect.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We were hiking when it started to snow.
We hiked when it was starting to snow.
We were hike when it started to snow.
We hiking were when it started to snow.
questions.explanation: Past continuous (background) + past simple (interrupting event): 'We were hiking when it started to snow.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: This trail is more difficult than the last one.
This trail is difficulter than the last one.
This trail is most difficult than the last one.
This trail is difficult than the last one.
questions.explanation: Long adjectives use 'more' for comparatives: 'more difficult than'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: This is the farest beach from the city.
This is the most far beach from the city.
This is the farthest beach from the city.
This is farthest beach from the city.
questions.explanation: Irregular superlative of 'far' is 'the farthest': 'the farthest beach'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Can I take a break, I feel exhausted?
Can I to take a break, I feel exhausted?
Can I taking a break, I feel exhausted?
I can take a break, I feel exhausted can?
questions.explanation: 'Can' is followed by the base form of the verb: 'Can I take a break?'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: You need to drink more water in this heat.
You need drink more water in this heat.
You needs to drink more water in this heat.
You need to drinking more water in this heat.
questions.explanation: 'Need to' + base verb expresses necessity: 'need to drink'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: He must have forgot his jacket, it's freezing outside.
He must have forgotten his jacket, it's freezing outside.
He must has forgotten his jacket, it's freezing outside.
He must forgotten his jacket, it's freezing outside.
questions.explanation: 'Must have' + past participle expresses a logical past conclusion: 'must have forgotten'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Are you going to join the hiking club?
Are you go to join the hiking club?
Do you going to join the hiking club?
Are you going join the hiking club?
questions.explanation: Question form: Are/Is + subject + going to + base verb: 'Are you going to join...?'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If the weather improves, we will go camping.
If the weather will improve, we go camping.
If the weather improves, we go will camping.
If the weather improved, we will go camping.
questions.explanation: First conditional: If + present simple, will + base verb: 'If the weather improves, we will go camping.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I don't mind waiting for the bus in the rain.
I don't mind to wait for the bus in the rain.
I don't mind wait for the bus in the rain.
I don't mind waited for the bus in the rain.
questions.explanation: 'Mind' is followed by a gerund (-ing form): 'don't mind waiting'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We hope visiting the mountains next month.
We hope to visit the mountains next month.
We hope visit the mountains next month.
We hope for visit the mountains next month.
questions.explanation: 'Hope' is followed by the infinitive with 'to': 'hope to visit'.

questions.question: We didn't take ___ luggage for the trip.
options: many
much
a lot
several
questions.explanation: 'Luggage' is uncountable, so use 'much' in negative sentences.

questions.question: There are ___ tourists at the beach this early in the morning.
options: a little
a few
much
little
questions.explanation: 'Tourists' is countable, and 'a few' means 'a small number of'.

questions.question: Choose the sentence that correctly uses 'while'.
options: While I was packing, my sister was checking the tickets.
While I was packing, but my sister checked the tickets.
I was packing while, my sister was checking the tickets.
While packing was I, my sister checking tickets.
questions.explanation: 'While' connects two actions happening at the same time: 'While I was packing, my sister was checking the tickets.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We'll leave as soon as the rain stops.
We'll leave as soon as the rain will stop.
We'll leave as soon the rain stops as.
We'll leave as soon as the rain stopped.
questions.explanation: 'As soon as' + present simple is used to talk about the near future: 'as soon as the rain stops.'

questions.question: We stopped for lunch ___ the airport.
options: on the way to
on the way for
in the way to
at the way to
questions.explanation: 'On the way to' + place describes stopping during a journey: 'on the way to the airport.'

questions.question: It stayed sunny ___ the whole trip.
options: throughout
during of
along
across
questions.explanation: 'Throughout' means 'during the entire period of': 'throughout the whole trip.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence. (Direct: "I will call you tomorrow.")
options: She said that she will call me tomorrow.
She said that she would call me the next day.
She said that she would call me tomorrow.
She said she calling me the next day.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, 'will' shifts to 'would' and 'tomorrow' shifts to 'the next day'.

questions.question: Which is the correct way to start an email to a friend telling them about your holiday plans?
options: Dear Sir/Madam,
Hey Kamran,
To Whom It May Concern,
Dear Customer,
questions.explanation: 'Hey [Name],' is a friendly, informal greeting suitable for a close friend.

questions.question: Which is the correct way to end an email to a friend before a trip?
options: Yours faithfully,
See you soon,
Sincerely,
Regards,
questions.explanation: 'See you soon,' is a warm, informal closing suitable for a friend before meeting up.

questions.question: Choose the correct suggestion.
options: Shall we book the tickets online?
Shall we booking the tickets online?
Shall we to book the tickets online?
We shall booked the tickets online?
questions.explanation: 'Shall we' + base verb is used to make a suggestion: 'Shall we book...?'

questions.question: Which sentence correctly combines 'This is the season.' and 'I enjoy the season the most.'?
options: This is the season who I enjoy the most.
This is the season which I enjoy the most.
This is the season where I enjoy the most.
This is the season what I enjoy the most.
questions.explanation: 'Which' is used for things in relative clauses: 'the season which I enjoy the most.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We always pack our bags the night before.
We pack always our bags the night before.
Always we pack our bags the night before always.
We pack our bags always the night before.
questions.explanation: Adverbs of frequency usually go before the main verb: 'We always pack our bags.'

questions.question: Which sentence has correct punctuation?
options: Do you know where the nearest pharmacy is?
Do you know where is the nearest pharmacy?
Do you know where the nearest pharmacy is.
Do you know, where the nearest pharmacy is?
questions.explanation: Indirect questions keep normal word order and end with a question mark: 'where the nearest pharmacy is?'

questions.question: I ___ for this trip for weeks, so I'm really excited.
options: plan
have planned
have been planning
planned
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous emphasizes duration of an ongoing action: 'have been planning'.

questions.question: This suitcase isn't ours, it's ___.
options: you
your
yours
your's
questions.explanation: Possessive pronoun (stands alone, no noun after it): 'it's yours.'

questions.question: Choose the sentence that correctly uses sequencing words.
options: First, check in. After that, find your gate. Finally, board the plane.
First check in after that find gate finally board plane.
Finally check in, first find your gate, after that board.
After that first check in, finally find gate board plane.
questions.explanation: Sequencing words 'First,', 'After that,' and 'Finally,' organize steps clearly with commas.

questions.question: Every passenger ___ to show their ticket at the gate.
options: need
needs
needing
are needing
questions.explanation: 'Every' takes a singular verb: 'Every passenger needs...'

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag.
options: You've packed your passport, haven't you?
You've packed your passport, have you?
You've packed your passport, didn't you?
You've packed your passport, haven't?
questions.explanation: Positive statement + negative tag: 'You've packed your passport, haven't you?'
